purpose: Validate automatic AVX2/FMA eight-unit recognition scheduling across dense model sizes, sparse/mixed inputs, and shared-pool concurrency.

build: cargo build --release --locked --example cpu_benchmark; default features; no profiling or custom Rust flags
retained_change: Extend the existing eight-owner automatic NEON recognition policy to AVX2/FMA when context capacity >= 8 and independent recognition units >= 8; explicit limits and other backends retain their selection. Batches count as one unit.

validation.within_process_owned_outputs_equal: Each worker checks cold, warm-up and all measured owned outputs, including both simultaneous requests.
validation.alignment_capture: Enabled in synthetic integration checks; disabled in real-model benchmark jobs.

limitations: Seven cases, three distinct inputs, one eight-logical-CPU affinity mask, one first batch, one warm-up and three measured batches per case/version; no automatic repetitions or retries.
No C# comparison, full corpus, full 36-cell performance qualification, ARM64/AVX-512 hardware validation, or performance validation of other context capacities.
Tiny sparse uses the unchanged three-active-owner policy; its faster candidate sample is not attributed to recognition scheduling. Retained activation and workspace are identical.
Tiny concurrent ranges overlap; throughput benefit is inconclusive. Medium concurrent reduction is small (1.7%) and not a statistical significance claim.
Medium single-request baseline samples drift upward; three samples do not establish steady state or a universal speedup.
More owners increase retained per-request memory; peak private commit includes loading/first-use and is not working set.

Baseline executable was reused from the prior stage analysis; old timings are not pooled with this comparison. Its prior original-harness worker execution was 7.16 seconds, and this comparison adds 16.2854323 seconds, still below 60 seconds.
The pre-existing Windows UNBOUND_AFFINITY unused-import warning remains.
